rationale: A TUPLE-typed using alias, plus the malformed directive that made the same position publish its own ALIAS. `using Named = (Type ContainerType, string FieldName);` declares a dependency on a tuple TYPE, and a tuple type's identity is its element TYPES — `(Type ContainerType, string FieldName)` and `(Type, string)` are the same type and the element names are only labels this declaration gives them. The raw text therefore published two names that are not part of the type, in the one position whose contract says the published value is a NAME (the D3 rule, which already strips a generic alias's arguments and already strips element names from a tuple ARGUMENT). FOUND BY AN INDEPENDENT DERIVATION rather than by a failing fixture: cs-ont-08 disagreed with the analyzer on exactly ONE row out of 2,185 imports over 800 aspnetcore `src` files — src/Components/Endpoints/src/Forms/ClientValidationCache.cs:17, analyzer `(Type ContainerType,string FieldName)` — so both the corpus measurement and the direction of the fix come from a source neither side authored. `Named` and `Unnamed` are the SAME type written two ways and must publish ONE string; that pair is the pin. `OneElement` is the second half: `(string Only)` is not a C# type at all (there is no one-element tuple), the grammar parks `= (string Only)` in an ERROR node, the `=` stops being a direct child so the alias form is undetectable — and the analyzer then published the ALIAS `OneElement` as the dependency with `importKind: namespace`, which is the CSD7/R1 fabrication this lane has already paid for once. An unparsed directive now publishes nothing AND reports a ParseError, because the skip also skips the child walk where ERROR nodes become warnings: with the skip alone, measured `errors: []` on a file whose directive did not parse. `Generic` is the control that the pre-existing D3 rule still holds — arguments stripped off the module and published as their own `references` rows, never welded in — and it is also why `string` is pinned by its ABSENCE there: a predefined type contributes nothing (the grammar's own tag), so `Dictionary<string, Widget>` publishes `Widget` and not `string`.

`using Named = (Type ContainerType, string FieldName);` — element NAMES dropped, because they are not part of the tuple type
a qualified element keeps its path: the rule strips element names, not namespaces

and the SAME string for the tuple written without element names — one type, one name, which is the property the pre-fix value could not hold

D3's half: the arguments are dependencies in their own right and are published beside the module edge. `reference_qualified`, NOT `import_based` — an argument is a TYPE reference, not a namespace import. `string` is deliberately absent: a predefined type contributes nothing (the grammar's own tag), which is why `Dictionary<string, Widget>` publishes `Widget` and not `string`.

forbidImports.note: THE FABRICATION THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR. A directive that did not parse must not publish its own alias as the dependency. C# has no one-element tuple, so `(string Only)` cannot be a target; the analyzer published `OneElement` — a name the file imports nothing from.
same row, stated by its published spelling
the pre-fix spelling: element names welded onto the module
and the un-normalised spelling of it, which is the raw source text — pinned because the first draft of this instrument's own truth derived exactly this string and disagreed with the analyzer on it
the module edge never carries its arguments (D3)

expectErrors.note: THE DIRECTIVE THAT DID NOT PARSE IS REPORTED, not silently skipped. `using OneElement = (string Only);` is line 32 and there is no C# one-element tuple, so the grammar parks `= (string Only)` in an ERROR node. The skip that avoids publishing the alias also skips the child walk where ERROR nodes become ParseError warnings, so with the skip alone this file reported `errors: []` — a silent parse failure. Pinning the error is what makes 'publish nothing' an honest silence rather than a lost row.
